analysis.title: BP beats, XOM & CVX cancel on ADIPEC, ME escalation risk + Energy Daily 30/10/26
key_insights: Brent touched a 6-month high above $117/b on 30 Oct on fresh attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy assets, with no progress in diplomacy with Iran. Iran says it will engage only if the US lifts the blockade on Iranian oil and unfreezes Iranian funds.

The UBS specialist salesperson (Dominic Ellis) believes the market is not realistically pricing the medium or longer-term impact of the Middle East conflict, and that prices could spike higher without more substantive diplomatic progress. Spot and the front of the curve price a higher chance of escalation and disruption.

WSJ reports President Trump continues to take briefings on military options for Iran and has signalled attacks may restart after the US midterms on Tuesday 3 Nov. The author does not expect the midterms to catalyse renewed US diplomacy with Iran, whatever the outcome.
Exxon and Chevron executives pulled out of ADIPEC in Abu Dhabi next week, citing security concerns (Reuters). Exxon CEO Darren Woods and Chevron upstream president Clay Neff had been due to attend.

BP 3Q beat: 10% ahead of consensus at operating level, 15% ahead on adjusted net income and 11% on net cash flow ex working capital, despite a sharp rise in consensus after the trading update. There was no surprise on shareholder cash returns, a minor near-term negative.

New BP CEO Meg O'Neil set 4 strategic priorities, including using excess cash to accelerate settling remaining Macondo liabilities (~$5bn). The 15 Dec capital markets day is the next catalyst, where the author expects BP to update on buybacks within its financial framework.

Specialist investors see BP as the integrated energy name with the most positive fundamental change this year, and the author expects positioning and performance to improve relative to Shell and TTE before the CMD. Generalists who rotated out after Chair Albert Manifold left are not yet ready to return.

Trading desk: EStoxx -45bps at the open as the AI unwind resumed after the US close. Nasdaq futures are -1.9% after AMZN (-7%) missed on AWS growth and margins and INTC (-23%) beat but guided light on supply constraints. SNDK beat offers little offset.

The desk estimates the futures implied move at ~80bps from index weights alone, so contagion risk across the AI complex is evident. NVDA is -1.6% after hours and neoclouds are all lower. The weekend question is orderly rotation into defensives and value versus a broad de-gross across momentum and equities.

Prior session had Value outperforming Growth by 2.7% and Consumer Staples (+1.6%) beating the SOX (-1.4%). MDLZ is +7.6% after hours on results. Asia is lower in pockets, with the Hang Seng (+1.4%) the regional outlier.

BoJ held 8-1 with a modestly hawkish tone, keeping a December hike in play. FY2027 core CPI forecast was raised to 2.6% versus UBS's 2.5%, FY2027 growth is 0.7%, the proposed food-tax cut was excluded from forecasts, and ETF disposals accelerate from January 2027.
Yen is firmer near 157.60/USD within a broad dollar sell-off, with CHF topping the G10 board on haven demand. The US 10yr yield is 4.92% (-2bps), extending Thursday's rally.

WTI briefly broke $105 before settling near $103 after Iran signalled no change in its peace-deal terms. The desk says the energy risk premium stays embedded into the weekend, and a few dollars either way on crude has had muted impact on equities so far.

European flows on Thursday were balanced (50/50). Banks were 17% of turnover and better to buy on Spanish names. Technology (16%) saw semis supply, Healthcare (15%) saw demand, and Energy and Basic Resources saw supply.

QatarEnergy is buying long-term US and other LNG as a hedge that would generate revenue if Hormuz exports are disrupted. It signed a 20-year deal for 3 mtpa from Woodside's Louisiana LNG and up to 4 mtpa from Cheniere through 2054, 7 mtpa in two weeks, making it the largest buyer of US LNG.

Cheniere raised its full-year earnings forecast on higher LNG export volumes, lifted its quarterly dividend by more than 12% to 62.5 cents, and shares rose 5%. Middle East disruption is pushing buyers toward US LNG.
European gas front-month touched €100/MWh on Wednesday for the first time since December 2022. Italy blames German storage-filling delays, and governments are under pressure to cut household costs.

Ukraine has paused strikes on Russian refineries after pressure from Trump (WSJ), expected to last until after the midterms and possibly deeper into November. Russia will extend its diesel export ban to year-end with quotas to meet a US supply deal, and refinery utilisation rose 25% in October as drone attacks subsided.

The US is lending a final ~40 million barrels from the SPR under the global IEA deal, bringing the SPR to its lowest level since 1982. Heavy reliance on the SPR has reduced its ability to calm markets.
Refiners are raising dividends: Delek Logistics lifted its quarterly dividend ~18% to $0.30, the fourth refiner to raise in two weeks after PSX (Oct 16), MPC (Oct 28) and PBF (Oct 29).

European integrateds 3Q: UBS expects Shell shares to outperform on a larger buyback, TotalEnergies results were close to expectations with a PT raise, Repsol beat with a higher-than-expected buyback, and OMV had a 28% CFFO beat but a chemicals drag.

Oilfield services and midstream: TechnipFMC 3Q EBITDA beat Street by 5% but subsea orders were well below expectations, and it added four subsea opportunities worth over $3bn to a ~$32.1bn target list. DT Midstream raised its 2026 EBITDA guide. EPD and PBF beat.

PetroChina nine-month net profit hit an all-time high of Rmb155.8bn while oil and gas output slipped slightly on Middle East disruption to overseas crude production. SK Innovation 3Q operating profit beat UBS by 88% on refining and lubricants.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q beat of 10% at operating level, 15% on adjusted NI and 11% on net CF ex WC. The desk sees BP delivering the most positive fundamental change among integrateds this year, and expects relative improvement versus Shell and TTE into the 15 Dec CMD.
UBS Research expects the shares to outperform given the larger increase to buybacks, with durability the key issue now.
UBS raises its price target after a strong 3Q26 and positive comments on CFFO. A separate preview-style note expected a neutral reaction as results and guidance were close to expectations.
Neste: strong 3Q and improved utilisation offset Rotterdam expansion delays. UBS retains Buy and a €38 PT.
OMV: new PT of €79 per share. Very strong cash flow with a 28% CFFO beat, but a larger drag from chemicals (34% of EV) may dampen sentiment.
Technip Energies: price target raised on greater visibility around the margin recovery.
3Q26 EBITDA beat Street by 5% but subsea orders came in well below expectations. UBS stays positive on a visible offshore upcycle and margin growth through the end of the decade.
Cheniere raised guidance and its dividend and stepped up buybacks in 3Q26.
PBF reported a big 3Q26 beat, continued to lower debt and raised its dividend.
Enterprise Products Partners reported a 3Q26 beat.
Strong 3Q with the 2026 EBITDA guide raised and MIST plus 2 other projects reaching FID.
UBS sees an improving forward outlook and an FCF growth inflection underway.
3Q26 earnings beat with a strong 2027 outlook across US drilling and completions.
ADNOC Drilling: UBS turns more cautious on 2027 but increases estimates in later years after results and a strategic update.

sector_views.rationale: The desk expects BP to improve relative to Shell and TTE into its CMD and sees Shell shares outperforming on a bigger buyback. The sector has delivered mostly positive 3Q cash-return surprises, and BP's lack of one is a minor negative.
Middle East supply disruption is pushing buyers, including QatarEnergy, to US LNG. Cheniere, DT Midstream and EPD all beat or raised.
Four refiners raised dividends in two weeks (PSX, MPC, PBF, DK) and SK Innovation beat on refining strength.
TechnipFMC sees a visible offshore upcycle, but order timing is a near-term concern after subsea orders missed.
The desk flags an AI unwind after hyperscaler earnings and capex guidance disappointed, with risk of further rotation into value and defensives or a broader de-gross.

earnings_insights: BP 3Q26 (reported 30 Oct): 10% ahead of consensus at operating level, 15% ahead on adjusted net income and 11% ahead on net cash flow ex working capital. No cash-return surprise.

AMZN (-7% after hours) missed on AWS growth and margins per the UBS desk. INTC (-23% after hours) beat on the quarter but guided light on supply constraints. SNDK beat. MDLZ +7.6% after hours on results.
OMV 3Q26 (UBS preview-style take): CFFO beat of 28% against consensus, offset by a larger drag from chemicals (34% of EV).
SK Innovation 3Q operating profit of W3.7tn beat UBS by 88% and consensus by 69%, on refining and lubricant strength.
TechnipFMC 3Q26 EBITDA beat Street by 5% but subsea orders were well below expectations.
Cheniere raised its full-year earnings forecast and its quarterly dividend by more than 12% to 62.5 cents per share.
PetroChina nine-month 2026 net profit reached Rmb155.8bn, an all-time high for the period.
Repsol 3Q26: earnings and CFFO ex-WC above consensus, buyback raised more than expected, updated 2026 guidance supportive.
TotalEnergies 3Q26: UBS expects a neutral reaction, results and guidance close to expectations and the buyback only slightly ahead. Technip Energies 3Q26 in line with guidance confirmed.
DNO sold Kurdistan crude locally at an average $38.5/bbl in 3Q versus $31.2 a year earlier, with gross production of 77,621 bopd across Tawke and Peshkabir.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A 6-month high on attacks on vessels in Hormuz and Saudi assets. The author expects further upside without diplomatic progress.
The energy risk premium stays embedded into the weekend, with muted equity impact from a few dollars either way.
Extends Thursday's rally and provides some support to equities.
Yen firmer after the BoJ's hawkish hold, within a broad dollar sell-off.
Firmer inflation guidance keeps a December BoJ hike in play.
Slightly soft growth, but policy normalisation continues.
Highest since December 2022, raising political pressure on energy costs.
Slight build led by clean distillates.
Heavy SPR lending has reduced the US ability to calm oil markets.

risk_factors: Escalation in the Middle East, including a restart of US military action against Iran after the 3 Nov midterms and further attacks on Hormuz shipping or Saudi assets.
A broader de-gross across momentum and equities if the AI unwind continues after hyperscaler earnings and capex guidance disappointments.
Oil prices could spike higher if the market is underpricing the medium to longer-term impact of the conflict.
Absence of a shareholder-return surprise at BP, and generalist reluctance to return before the 15 Dec CMD.
Subsea order timing at TechnipFMC and Rotterdam expansion delays at Neste.
European gas supply stress into winter, with storage-filling delays and prices at €100/MWh.
vol_and_positioning: The UBS desk estimates the Nasdaq futures implied move at ~80bps on index weights alone after AMZN and INTC prints, with contagion risk across the AI complex.
Value outperformed Growth by 2.7% on Thursday and Consumer Staples (+1.6%) beat the SOX (-1.4%), pointing to a rotation out of AI-linked names.
Thursday flows in Europe were balanced 50/50 with elevated turnover. Banks were better to buy on Spanish names, semis saw supply and Energy saw supply.
Generalist investors who rotated out of BP after the Chair's departure are not yet ready to return, while specialists are mostly on board.
geopolitical: US-Iran: the Hormuz blockade, attacks on vessels and Saudi energy assets, Vance's letter to Iranian officials with no response yet, Iranian conditions of lifting the blockade on Iranian oil and unfreezing funds, and Trump signalling attacks may restart after the US midterms on 3 Nov.

Ukraine has paused strikes on Russian refineries after pressure from Trump, while Russia has stepped up attacks on Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure and renewed efforts to revive US-backed peace talks continue.
Russia will extend its diesel export ban to year-end with quotas to meet its export commitment to the US under an energy ceasefire deal agreed after a Putin-Trump call.
Greek PM Mitsotakis called for a global maritime truce after a drone attack sank a Greek container ship off Bulgaria, one of a series of strikes on ships in the western Black Sea this month.
Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez said the government is identifying state assets to offer to the private sector or return to former owners.
The Iran war has disrupted Qatari LNG output, and the Hormuz blockade and war damage are cited as the reason QatarEnergy is buying US LNG.

tension_points.theme: oil risk premium and Iran escalation
tension_points.bull_case: Spot and the front of the curve already price a higher probability of escalation, but the author believes the medium and longer-term impact is not priced and prices could spike higher without substantive diplomatic progress.
tension_points.bear_case: A few dollars either way on crude has had muted impact on equity markets so far, and a diplomatic breakthrough (Iran engaging if the US lifts the blockade and unfreezes funds) would remove the premium.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More substantive evidence of diplomatic progress between the US and Iran than so far, such as the US committing to lift the blockade on Iranian oil and unfreeze Iranian funds.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower yields provide support and the move could be an orderly rotation into defensives and value, as seen with Value beating Growth by 2.7% on Thursday.
tension_points.bear_case: Contagion from AMZN and INTC after-hours moves and Nasdaq futures at -1.9% could become a broader de-gross across momentum and equities.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market is not realistically pricing the medium or longer-term impact of the Middle East conflict, and prices could spike higher without diplomatic progress.
